# the contributor audit: positive energy charts and failed arithmetic-filtered escorts

## Finite-hull positive chart

Full PASS for
`candidate c0fc791108fc8765`.
Envelope differentiation gives the positive sign and factor(d+1)/d in
the energy-root gradient. Its own-fiber concavity tangent implies the
optimizing denominator's uniform lower bound1/(d+1).

The finite support LP formula for real sections is exact. Its dual is
pointed because the fixed affine rows span the base affine hull. Every
optimal face has a vertex; the finitely many independent row inverses
give slopes bounded uniformly in the continuous normal. The section
support functions, hence the sections, are uniformly Hausdorff-Lipschitz
even at boundary bases. Support inequalities turn that estimate into
a common source-centered interior ball for nearby sections.

The subsequent local energy estimate tests attained minimizers in each
other's bodies, using their uniform parameter and denominator bounds.
Symmetric-difference volume control follows from a common inner ball
and dilations. The finite Lipschitz convex infimal-convolution extension
equals minus the energy on its local convex domain, so a finite
subgradient supplies the required boundary support. Concavity along
segments extends the local support globally. This is not an unsupported
boundary-supergradient claim for arbitrary ambient bodies.

The shorter support-majorant construction has the correct PLUS sign
in b.(z-p). It directly retains the source denominator and its positive
lower bound on the whole finite hull. It need not be the energy
supergradient chart. The square-root-radius counterexample correctly
separates these two conclusions for noncanonical bodies.
Nothing in this argument bounds original cap loss or continuation cost.

## Base entropy versus retained mass

Full direct calculations in
`candidate 2b7d1c7e003a98d0` PASS.
The boundary-face full infimum is genuinely unattained, while the
face-restricted objective is strictly convex and attained. Holder gives
the exact attained Renyi dual. E>=T uses the density ceiling only for
the retained submeasure, not for the escort; equality forces the full
minimal-face mass and its actual mean. The tangent-defect inequality
has the correct direction because the corresponding hinge dual value
is at least T. Its positive excess cannot be counted as retained mass.

The max-E occupied-parity bound explicitly depends on the archived
weighted integer-centerpoint theorem; it is not a new arithmetic bridge.
Its strict equality classification likewise retains that theorem's
strict minimal-face refinement as a dependency. No new OC inference
is made from these scalar comparisons.

## Unique weighted-centerpoint escort failures

Full PASS for
`candidate 9a6be4fc7a226f55`.
The endpoint Minkowski midpoint intervals are exactly those stated and
are contained in the middle cube. Hence every fiber is actual. All
individual masses are below half the total, the unique qualifying
weighted base-centerpoint is zero, and the centroid graph is nonaffine.
The escort point formulas have exponents d+2 as required.

The displayed oblique cap captures all of the small endpoint, none of
the other endpoint, and a proper middle interval. Its exact normalized
masses991/4012<1/4 and8099/36838<2/9 follow. The separate middle-cube
center retains the whole cube and a reflected endpoint pair, giving
all-halfspace lower bounds5/17 and83/326. Thus both selector failures
are rigorous and do not concern existence in OC. the contributor reran44 checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
